1. Identity and Precise Coordinates
Grant Road is a locality situated within the south mumbai micro-region of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. Its generated reference coordinate is approximately 18.9491 degrees north latitude and 72.8045 degrees east longitude (verifiable and refinable through Nominatim and the OpenStreetMap node/way database, using the Geofabrik Maharashtra extract as the base layer). The area sits at an estimated mean elevation of about 223.2 metres above mean sea level, derived from the NASADEM / SRTM 30-metre digital elevation model and cross-checked against ALOS AW3D where finer relief is required. The character of Grant Road is shaped by its position: The southern tip of Salsette Island / original Seven Islands: Colaba, Mazagaon, Parel, Mahim, etc.

2. Etymology, History and Civic Evolution
The name Grant Road carries layers of civic memory. Historically part of the larger Salsette and Konkan settlement network, the place grew through phases of fishing-village economy, colonial port expansion, post-1960 industrialisation, and post-1990 planned node development under agencies such as CIDCO, MIDC and the Municipal Corporations of Greater Mumbai, Thane, Bhiwandi-Nizampur, Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Panvel. Oral histories, Marathi and Gujarati street names, and colonial survey maps (available via Wikidata and old Survey of India sheets) anchor the local identity. The agent should respect the real demographic layering when populating Grant Road, drawing on census ward maps and OSM landuse polygons.

3. Topography, Soil and Geology
Geologically Grant Road rests on Deccan Trap basalt of the late Cretaceous, overlain in low pockets by alluvium, marine clay and laterite. The terrain here is noticeably hilly, with paddy fields on reclaimed lowlands as the dominant ground cover and MS lattices and corrugated sheeting forming the typical structural palette. Slope gradients should be sampled from the Copernicus DEM so that roads, drains and foundations follow believable contours; the agent must bake normal maps from the elevation mesh to give every lane and nullah a physically consistent fall toward the nearest creek or storm drain.

4. Hydrography and Proximity to Creeks, Rivers and the Sea
The hydrography around Grant Road is governed by the regional creek and river network: the Ulhas estuary gives rise to Vasai Creek in the north and Thane Creek in the east, while the Arabian Sea bounds the west and the Uran/Sheva and Karanja creeks shape the Raigad shore. Within Grant Road, storm-water nullahs, tidal inlets, ponds and (where present) mangrove fringes must be modelled from OSM water and natural=wetland polygons. The agent should render the slopes that shed water into the mangrove behaviour of water during the monsoon and spring tide, and must keep restricted naval and port waters (Butcher Island, Middle Ground, Oyster Rock, JNPT channel) marked as no-go zones using Indian Navy Notices to Mariners.

5. Climate and Local Microclimate
Grant Road experiences a tropical monsoon climate (Koppen Aw). A typical atmospheric moment here is a cool December nor'easter off the sea. Microclimatic variation is real: creek-side and reclaimed lowlands are cooler and breezier, while dense concrete cores trap heat; the agent should drive a local temperature and humidity field from landuse (water, forest, built-up) so that the player feels the sweat and railway-platform tea of each pocket.

Even inside the city, Girgaon keeps a wild edge: casuarina windbreaks along the coast, and - where the location borders Tungareshwar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Karnala or the creek mangroves - leopards, monkeys, peacocks, flamingos, kingfishers and crocodiles. The agent should seed fauna with believable ranges and schedules (flamingos in the Thane Creek flats, peacocks in Kharghar hills, leopards on the SGNP fringe) so the boundary between metropolis and wilderness is thin and thrilling, exactly as in the real region.

17. Human Density, NPC Archetypes and Crowd Physics
Population pressure in Girgaon is intense. The agent must support thousands of concurrently simulated pedestrians with social-force crowd physics: a migrant labourer waiting for a contract truck jostles through a junction, commuters flow toward the station at 8 am, festival processions block roads, and personal-space bubbles part and re-form. Each NPC needs a simple daily routine (home-sleep, commute, work, market, leisure) drawn from the local economy so the crowd is purposeful, not random. LOD must cull and simplify distant crowds to hold framerate.

18. Vehicle Presence, Traffic AI and Parking
The road life of Girgaon is a choreography of cycle-wallahs with wholesale cloth. The agent needs a traffic micro-simulation: signal logic at junctions, lane discipline (loose), honking behaviour, overtaking on the wrong side, jaywalking pressure, and parking on footpaths. Heavy JNPT container trucks, BEST/NMMT buses, autos, two-wheelers, tempos and private cars each need distinct mass, acceleration and braking so the feel differs by vehicle class. Congestion should emerge from geometry, not scripting.

19. Implementation Notes for the Building Agent (data, mesh, texture, LOD)
To realise Girgaon faithfully, the building agent should: (a) pull the OSM relation/way for 'Girgaon' via Overpass using its bounding box; (b) clip the NASADEM 30 m and Copernicus DEM 10 m tiles to that box for terrain; (c) import building footprints from OSM + Microsoft Building Footprints and extrude to heights from OSM building:levels or a learned prior; (d) texture from Sentinel-2/Landsat seasonal composites and Mapillary street-level photos; (e) place vegetation, water and landmarks from OSM natural/water/amenity tags; (f) bake lighting and occlusion; and (g) stream the result with a quadtree LOD so the 1,000+ km2 region stays playable. Every coordinate should be re-verifiable against OpenStreetMap (planet.osm / Geofabrik Maharashtra extract) for roads, buildings, landuse, water, railways; the Overpass API (overpass-api.de / kumi.systems mirror) for targeted queries such as 'way["natural"="water"] (bbox)' and 'relation["route"="railway"]'; Nominatim for geocoding place names to coordinates; OpenTopography and NASADEM / SRTM 30m & 90m for elevation meshes; ALOS AW3D and Copernicus DEM where finer detail is needed; Natural Earth (1:10m coastline, roads, populated places) for the regional frame; Wikidata and Wikipedia dumps for landmark metadata; OpenAddress and Microsoft Building Footprints for parcel and roof data; Mapillary and OpenAerialMap and Sentinel-2 / Landsat-8 for imagery-derived textures; the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Applications Centre and CIDCO planning maps for node layouts; the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) and Indian Navy Notices to Mariners for restricted zones; and the Free Map Tools / bboxfinder.com for coordinate verification..

20. Player Experience Brief for Girgaon
When the player arrives in Girgaon, the intended feeling is recognition: the salt wind, the specific skyline, the exact slant of the flyover, the smell of diesel and hot asphalt, the sound of the putter of a fishing boat engine. The agent must not abstract this place into a generic city; it must be unmistakably Girgaon, a slice of the real Konkan coast rendered at human scale, where one can walk, drive, sail or fly and feel the weight of a living, sweating, praying, working megacity that happens to sit on an island joined to the mainland only by bridges, creeks and causeways.


================================================================================
LOCATION DOSSIER: Kalbadevi  (south mumbai)
================================================================================

1. Identity and Precise Coordinates
Kalbadevi is a locality situated within the south mumbai micro-region of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. Its generated reference coordinate is approximately 18.9807 degrees north latitude and 72.8027 degrees east longitude (verifiable and refinable through Nominatim and the OpenStreetMap node/way database, using the Geofabrik Maharashtra extract as the base layer). The area sits at an estimated mean elevation of about 385.6 metres above mean sea level, derived from the NASADEM / SRTM 30-metre digital elevation model and cross-checked against ALOS AW3D where finer relief is required. The character of Kalbadevi is shaped by its position: The southern tip of Salsette Island / original Seven Islands: Colaba, Mazagaon, Parel, Mahim, etc.

2. Etymology, History and Civic Evolution
The name Kalbadevi carries layers of civic memory. Historically part of the larger Salsette and Konkan settlement network, the place grew through phases of fishing-village economy, colonial port expansion, post-1960 industrialisation, and post-1990 planned node development under agencies such as CIDCO, MIDC and the Municipal Corporations of Greater Mumbai, Thane, Bhiwandi-Nizampur, Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Panvel. Oral histories, Marathi and Gujarati street names, and colonial survey maps (available via Wikidata and old Survey of India sheets) anchor the local identity. The agent should respect the real demographic layering when populating Kalbadevi, drawing on census ward maps and OSM landuse polygons.

3. Topography, Soil and Geology
Geologically Kalbadevi rests on Deccan Trap basalt of the late Cretaceous, overlain in low pockets by alluvium, marine clay and laterite. The terrain here is a pronounced hill plateau, with salt-tolerant suru and palm belts as the dominant ground cover and mosaic tile and terrazzo thresholds forming the typical structural palette. Slope gradients should be sampled from the Copernicus DEM so that roads, drains and foundations follow believable contours; the agent must bake normal maps from the elevation mesh to give every lane and nullah a physically consistent fall toward the nearest creek or storm drain.

4. Hydrography and Proximity to Creeks, Rivers and the Sea
The hydrography around Kalbadevi is governed by the regional creek and river network: the Ulhas estuary gives rise to Vasai Creek in the north and Thane Creek in the east, while the Arabian Sea bounds the west and the Uran/Sheva and Karanja creeks shape the Raigad shore. Within Kalbadevi, storm-water nullahs, tidal inlets, ponds and (where present) mangrove fringes must be modelled from OSM water and natural=wetland polygons. The agent should render the slopes that shed water into the mangrove behaviour of water during the monsoon and spring tide, and must keep restricted naval and port waters (Butcher Island, Middle Ground, Oyster Rock, JNPT channel) marked as no-go zones using Indian Navy Notices to Mariners.

5. Climate and Local Microclimate
Kalbadevi experiences a tropical monsoon climate (Koppen Aw). Summers are hot and humid, the south-west monsoon from June to September delivers the bulk of ~2,200 mm annual rainfall, and winters are mild and dry. A typical atmospheric moment here is a October heat shimmer over the tar. Microclimatic variation is real: creek-side and reclaimed lowlands are cooler and breezier, while dense concrete cores trap heat; the agent should drive a local temperature and humidity field from landuse (water, forest, built-up) so that the player feels the the iron scent of a foundry of each pocket.

6. Urban Morphology and Street Grid
The built fabric of Kalbadevi follows a regular planned sector pattern. Primary movement is carried by crowded market gallis with hanging cables, with secondary lanes braiding into neighbourhood mazes. The agent must reconstruct the actual road graph from OSM highway tags (motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, service, living_street) and preserve one-way systems, foot-overbridges, level crossings and junction geometry. Where CIDCO planning exists (Vashi, Nerul, Kharghar, Panvel, Ulwe, Dronagiri), the sector grid with numbered sectors and central open spaces must be honoured exactly; where informal growth dominates (slum and warehouse belts), the organic, incremental lane network must be reproduced with believable dead-ends and shared courtyards.

7. Architecture and Built Form
Dominant construction in Kalbadevi is CAD-designed CIDCO plots with uniform setbacks, executed in mosaic tile and terrazzo thresholds. Façades range from weathered plaster stained by monsoon streaks to freshly painted societies in CIDCO pastels. Rooftops carry water tanks, antennae, solar heaters and pigeon coops; ground floors host shops, temples, garages and tea stalls. The agent should generate building footprints from Microsoft Building Footprints and OSM building polygons, extrude them using the SRTM/DEM ground height, and apply procedural façade rules (window rhythm, balcony rails, lorry loads, signage) so that no two streets look cloned. Heritage and Grade-I structures must use photogrammetry from Wikimedia/Mapillary rather than procedural approximation.

8. Landmarks, Civic Buildings and Public Realm
Anchoring the public realm of Kalbadevi is a crematorium on the creek edge, around which daily life orbits. Additional civic anchors include schools, dispensaries, ration shops, ration-dependent chawls, police chowkies, post offices, railway stations or bus depots, and religious structures of every denomination. The agent should place these from OSM amenity, shop, office, place_of_worship and public_transport tags, and give each a believable interior hint (a ticket counter, a stepwell, a bell) so the world reads as lived-in rather than a film set.

9. Markets, Commerce and the Informal Economy
Commerce in Kalbadevi is a stack of formal and informal layers: street vendors, weekly bazaars, kirana stores, wholesale markets (notably the APMC at Vashi and the power-loom/textile and warehouse economy of Bhiwandi), malls (Inorbit, Raghuleela, Little World, Viviana, Korum), and the heavy logistics of JNPT containers. The agent must simulate market rhythms - dawn fish auctions, midday lulls, evening crowding - with spawn tables tied to clock and weekday, and must scatter water tankers and mixer trucks as the prevalent moving load on the roads.

10. Residential Life, Communities and Daily Rhythm
The social texture of Kalbadevi is dominated by Marathi households from the Konkan, whose festivals, food and dress colour the streets. A typical figure one meets is a security guard in a booth. Homes are organised around shared wells, building compounds, chawl verandahs and society lawns; the agent should model domestic sound and smell (cooking, rangoli, drying clothes, evening prayers) as ambient layers so that the player, standing still, still receives a dense sense of neighbours. Caste, language and migrant geography should be readable in signage, shop names and the linguistic mix of NPC chatter.

11. Transport, Connectivity and Interchange
Mobility in and out of %s rides on the full Mumbai stack: the Western, Central and Harbour suburban railways; the Port line to Uran/JNPT; the Trans-Harbour and Panvel links; BEST, NMMT, TMT, KDMT and MSRTC buses; auto and taxi; the metro and monorail where built; and the road hierarchy from the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and NH-48/348 to the last village lane. The agent must lay track and stations from OSM railway geometries, animate trains on schedule, and let the player board, alight and transfer. Ferries connect koliwadas and islands (Gateway-Elephanta, Rewas-Mandwa, Uran creek boats), and a helipad/airport layer supports aerial movement.

12. Utilities, Drainage and Infrastructure
Under the surface of Kalbadevi runs a lattice of utilities: BMC/CMC water mains, sewer and stormwater nullahs, MSEB/Torrent power lines, gas pipelines, telecom ducts and CCTV. The agent should render manholes, transformer yards, overhead cable forests and pump houses, and must model the slopes that shed water into the mangrove that defines monsoon realism. Power-cut behaviour (generator hum, inverter beeps) should trigger on a believable schedule so the grid feels alive and fragile.

13. Soundscape and Smellscape
Stand in Kalbadevi and the ear receives the two-note horn of a BEST bus; the nose meets the iron scent of a foundry. These channels are as important as the visual for 'real-world feel'. The agent should build a 3D ambient audio system with distance attenuation, occlusion by buildings, and a diurnal mix (call to prayer, train horns, market cries, festival drums, aircraft on approach). A parallel smell/particulate layer (visible haze, incense, diesel) should tint the screen subtly so the player's senses are saturated the way a real Mumbaikar's are.

14. Day Cycle, Lighting and Night Behaviour
Light in Kalbadevi moves from harsh white noon to blue-white LED societies with motion sensors after dark. The agent must implement a physically based sun and moon arc for the latitude (19 N), with golden-hour warmth over the creek and blue-hour city glow. Night brings different NPC behaviour: food stalls ignite, watchmen patrol, lovers walk the sea face, and the port works in shifts. Neon, diya, tube-light and navigation lights must reflect off wet tar and water with believable bloom and caustics.

15. Monsoon, Tides and Flood Dynamics
The signature drama of Kalbadevi is water: slopes that shed water into the mangrove. The agent must couple a tidal model (semi-diurnal, ~4 m range in the Ulhas estuary) with a rainfall model (intensity curves from IMD climatology) so that low-lying reclamations, underbridges and creek edges flood realistically, while better-graded CIDCO nodes shed water. Mangrove belts should blunt wave energy; storm surge during cyclone alerts should temporarily submerge the lowest polygons. Pumps, sandbags and diverted traffic are part of the emergent gameplay.

Even inside the city, Kalbadevi keeps a wild edge: salt-tolerant suru and palm belts, and - where the location borders Tungareshwar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Karnala or the creek mangroves - leopards, monkeys, peacocks, flamingos, kingfishers and crocodiles. LOCATION DOSSIER: Crawford Market  (south mumbai)
================================================================================

1. Identity and Precise Coordinates
Crawford Market is a locality situated within the south mumbai micro-region of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. Its generated reference coordinate is approximately 18.9306 degrees north latitude and 72.8236 degrees east longitude (verifiable and refinable through Nominatim and the OpenStreetMap node/way database, using the Geofabrik Maharashtra extract as the base layer). The area sits at an estimated mean elevation of about 120.7 metres above mean sea level, derived from the NASADEM / SRTM 30-metre digital elevation model and cross-checked against ALOS AW3D where finer relief is required. The character of Crawford Market is shaped by its position: The southern tip of Salsette Island / original Seven Islands: Colaba, Mazagaon, Parel, Mahim, etc.

2. Etymology, History and Civic Evolution
The name Crawford Market carries layers of civic memory. Historically part of the larger Salsette and Konkan settlement network, the place grew through phases of fishing-village economy, colonial port expansion, post-1960 industrialisation, and post-1990 planned node development under agencies such as CIDCO, MIDC and the Municipal Corporations of Greater Mumbai, Thane, Bhiwandi-Nizampur, Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Panvel. Oral histories, Marathi and Gujarati street names, and colonial survey maps (available via Wikidata and old Survey of India sheets) anchor the local identity. The agent should respect the real demographic layering when populating Crawford Market, drawing on census ward maps and OSM landuse polygons.

3. Topography, Soil and Geology
Geologically Crawford Market rests on Deccan Trap basalt of the late Cretaceous, overlain in low pockets by alluvium, marine clay and laterite. The terrain here is noticeably hilly, with ornamental gulmohar and raintree avenues as the dominant ground cover and reinforced concrete with grey cement render forming the typical structural palette. Slope gradients should be sampled from the Copernicus DEM so that roads, drains and foundations follow believable contours; the agent must bake normal maps from the elevation mesh to give every lane and nullah a physically consistent fall toward the nearest creek or storm drain.

4. Hydrography and Proximity to Creeks, Rivers and the Sea
The hydrography around Crawford Market is governed by the regional creek and river network: the Ulhas estuary gives rise to Vasai Creek in the north and Thane Creek in the east, while the Arabian Sea bounds the west and the Uran/Sheva and Karanja creeks shape the Raigad shore. Within Crawford Market, storm-water nullahs, tidal inlets, ponds and (where present) mangrove fringes must be modelled from OSM water and natural=wetland polygons. The agent should render the creek-side encroachment that worsens every surge behaviour of water during the monsoon and spring tide, and must keep restricted naval and port waters (Butcher Island, Middle Ground, Oyster Rock, JNPT channel) marked as no-go zones using Indian Navy Notices to Mariners.

5. Climate and Local Microclimate
Crawford Market experiences a tropical monsoon climate (Koppen Aw). Summers are hot and humid, the south-west monsoon from June to September delivers the bulk of ~2,200 mm annual rainfall, and winters are mild and dry. A typical atmospheric moment here is the first thunderstorm of June. Microclimatic variation is real: creek-side and reclaimed lowlands are cooler and breezier, while dense concrete cores trap heat; the agent should drive a local temperature and humidity field from landuse (water, forest, built-up) so that the player feels the the iron scent of a foundry of each pocket.

6. Urban Morphology and Street Grid
The built fabric of Crawford Market follows a regular planned sector pattern. Primary movement is carried by seafront promenades with basalt bollards, with secondary lanes braiding into neighbourhood mazes. The agent must reconstruct the actual road graph from OSM highway tags (motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, service, living_street) and preserve one-way systems, foot-overbridges, level crossings and junction geometry. Where CIDCO planning exists (Vashi, Nerul, Kharghar, Panvel, Ulwe, Dronagiri), the sector grid with numbered sectors and central open spaces must be honoured exactly; where informal growth dominates (slum and warehouse belts), the organic, incremental lane network must be reproduced with believable dead-ends and shared courtyards.

7. Architecture and Built Form
Dominant construction in Crawford Market is warehouse godowns spanning acres, executed in reinforced concrete with grey cement render. Façades range from weathered plaster stained by monsoon streaks to freshly painted societies in CIDCO pastels. Rooftops carry water tanks, antennae, solar heaters and pigeon coops; ground floors host shops, temples, garages and tea stalls. The agent should generate building footprints from Microsoft Building Footprints and OSM building polygons, extrude them using the SRTM/DEM ground height, and apply procedural façade rules (window rhythm, balcony rails, lorry loads, signage) so that no two streets look cloned. Heritage and Grade-I structures must use photogrammetry from Wikimedia/Mapillary rather than procedural approximation.

8. Landmarks, Civic Buildings and Public Realm
Anchoring the public realm of Crawford Market is a mobile-tower lattice on a mast, around which daily life orbits. Additional civic anchors include schools, dispensaries, ration shops, ration-dependent chawls, police chowkies, post offices, railway stations or bus depots, and religious structures of every denomination. The agent should place these from OSM amenity, shop, office, place_of_worship and public_transport tags, and give each a believable interior hint (a ticket counter, a stepwell, a bell) so the world reads as lived-in rather than a film set.

9. Markets, Commerce and the Informal Economy
Commerce in Crawford Market is a stack of formal and informal layers: street vendors, weekly bazaars, kirana stores, wholesale markets (notably the APMC at Vashi and the power-loom/textile and warehouse economy of Bhiwandi), malls (Inorbit, Raghuleela, Little World, Viviana, Korum), and the heavy logistics of JNPT containers. The agent must simulate market rhythms - dawn fish auctions, midday lulls, evening crowding - with spawn tables tied to clock and weekday, and must scatter two-wheelers in triple formation as the prevalent moving load on the roads.

10. Residential Life, Communities and Daily Rhythm
The social texture of Crawford Market is dominated by Buddhist (Navayana) colonies, whose festivals, food and dress colour the streets. A typical figure one meets is a rag-picker with a jute sack. Homes are organised around shared wells, building compounds, chawl verandahs and society lawns; the agent should model domestic sound and smell (cooking, rangoli, drying clothes, evening prayers) as ambient layers so that the player, standing still, still receives a dense sense of neighbours. Caste, language and migrant geography should be readable in signage, shop names and the linguistic mix of NPC chatter.

11. Transport, Connectivity and Interchange
Mobility in and out of %s rides on the full Mumbai stack: the Western, Central and Harbour suburban railways; the Port line to Uran/JNPT; the Trans-Harbour and Panvel links; BEST, NMMT, TMT, KDMT and MSRTC buses; auto and taxi; the metro and monorail where built; and the road hierarchy from the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and NH-48/348 to the last village lane. The agent must lay track and stations from OSM railway geometries, animate trains on schedule, and let the player board, alight and transfer. Ferries connect koliwadas and islands (Gateway-Elephanta, Rewas-Mandwa, Uran creek boats), and a helipad/airport layer supports aerial movement.

12. Utilities, Drainage and Infrastructure
Under the surface of Crawford Market runs a lattice of utilities: BMC/CMC water mains, sewer and stormwater nullahs, MSEB/Torrent power lines, gas pipelines, telecom ducts and CCTV. The agent should render manholes, transformer yards, overhead cable forests and pump houses, and must model the creek-side encroachment that worsens every surge that defines monsoon realism. Power-cut behaviour (generator hum, inverter beeps) should trigger on a believable schedule so the grid feels alive and fragile.

13. Soundscape and Smellscape
Stand in Crawford Market and the ear receives the tinny speaker of a vada-pav cart; the nose meets the iron scent of a foundry. These channels are as important as the visual for 'real-world feel'. The agent should build a 3D ambient audio system with distance attenuation, occlusion by buildings, and a diurnal mix (call to prayer, train horns, market cries, festival drums, aircraft on approach). A parallel smell/particulate layer (visible haze, incense, diesel) should tint the screen subtly so the player's senses are saturated the way a real Mumbaikar's are.

14. Day Cycle, Lighting and Night Behaviour
Light in Crawford Market moves from harsh white noon to blue-white LED societies with motion sensors after dark. The agent must implement a physically based sun and moon arc for the latitude (19 N), with golden-hour warmth over the creek and blue-hour city glow. Night brings different NPC behaviour: food stalls ignite, watchmen patrol, lovers walk the sea face, and the port works in shifts. Neon, diya, tube-light and navigation lights must reflect off wet tar and water with believable bloom and caustics.

15. Monsoon, Tides and Flood Dynamics
The signature drama of Crawford Market is water: creek-side encroachment that worsens every surge. The agent must couple a tidal model (semi-diurnal, ~4 m range in the Ulhas estuary) with a rainfall model (intensity curves from IMD climatology) so that low-lying reclamations, underbridges and creek edges flood realistically, while better-graded CIDCO nodes shed water. Mangrove belts should blunt wave energy; storm surge during cyclone alerts should temporarily submerge the lowest polygons. Pumps, sandbags and diverted traffic are part of the emergent gameplay.

16. Vegetation, Wildlife and the Edge of the Wild
Even inside the city, Crawford Market keeps a wild edge: ornamental gulmohar and raintree avenues, and - where the location borders Tungareshwar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Karnala or the creek mangroves - leopards, monkeys, peacocks, flamingos, kingfishers and crocodiles. The agent should seed fauna with believable ranges and schedules (flamingos in the Thane Creek flats, peacocks in Kharghar hills, leopards on the SGNP fringe) so the boundary between metropolis and wilderness is thin and thrilling, exactly as in the real region.

17. Human Density, NPC Archetypes and Crowd Physics
Population pressure in Crawford Market is intense. The agent must support thousands of concurrently simulated pedestrians with social-force crowd physics: a rag-picker with a jute sack jostles through a junction, commuters flow toward the station at 8 am, festival processions block roads, and personal-space bubbles part and re-form. Each NPC needs a simple daily routine (home-sleep, commute, work, market, leisure) drawn from the local economy so the crowd is purposeful, not random. LOD must cull and simplify distant crowds to hold framerate.

18. Vehicle Presence, Traffic AI and Parking
The road life of Crawford Market is a choreography of two-wheelers in triple formation. The agent needs a traffic micro-simulation: signal logic at junctions, lane discipline (loose), honking behaviour, overtaking on the wrong side, jaywalking pressure, and parking on footpaths. Heavy JNPT container trucks, BEST/NMMT buses, autos, two-wheelers, tempos and private cars each need distinct mass, acceleration and braking so the feel differs by vehicle class. Congestion should emerge from geometry, not scripting.

19. Implementation Notes for the Building Agent (data, mesh, texture, LOD)
To realise Crawford Market faithfully, the building agent should: (a) pull the OSM relation/way for 'Crawford Market' via Overpass using its bounding box; (b) clip the NASADEM 30 m and Copernicus DEM 10 m tiles to that box for terrain; (c) import building footprints from OSM + Microsoft Building Footprints and extrude to heights from OSM building:levels or a learned prior; (d) texture from Sentinel-2/Landsat seasonal composites and Mapillary street-level photos; (e) place vegetation, water and landmarks from OSM natural/water/amenity tags; (f) bake lighting and occlusion; and (g) stream the result with a quadtree LOD so the 1,000+ km2 region stays playable. Every coordinate should be re-verifiable against OpenStreetMap (planet.osm / Geofabrik Maharashtra extract) for roads, buildings, landuse, water, railways; the Overpass API (overpass-api.de / kumi.systems mirror) for targeted queries such as 'way["natural"="water"] (bbox)' and 'relation["route"="railway"]'; Nominatim for geocoding place names to coordinates; OpenTopography and NASADEM / SRTM 30m & 90m for elevation meshes; ALOS AW3D and Copernicus DEM where finer detail is needed; Natural Earth (1:10m coastline, roads, populated places) for the regional frame; Wikidata and Wikipedia dumps for landmark metadata; OpenAddress and Microsoft Building Footprints for parcel and roof data; Mapillary and OpenAerialMap and Sentinel-2 / Landsat-8 for imagery-derived textures; the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Applications Centre and CIDCO planning maps for node layouts; the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) and Indian Navy Notices to Mariners for restricted zones; and the Free Map Tools / bboxfinder.com for coordinate verification..

20. Player Experience Brief for Crawford Market
When the player arrives in Crawford Market, the intended feeling is recognition: the salt wind, the specific skyline, the exact slant of the flyover, the smell of the iron scent of a foundry, the sound of the tinny speaker of a vada-pav cart. The agent must not abstract this place into a generic city; it must be unmistakably Crawford Market, a slice of the real Konkan coast rendered at human scale, where one can walk, drive, sail or fly and feel the weight of a living, sweating, praying, working megacity that happens to sit on an island joined to the mainland only by bridges, creeks and causeways.

The agent must reconstruct the actual road graph from OSM highway tags (motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, service, living_street) and preserve one-way systems, foot-overbridges, level crossings and junction geometry. Where CIDCO planning exists (Vashi, Nerul, Kharghar, Panvel, Ulwe, Dronagiri), the sector grid with numbered sectors and central open spaces must be honoured exactly; where informal growth dominates (slum and warehouse belts), the organic, incremental lane network must be reproduced with believable dead-ends and shared courtyards.

7. Architecture and Built Form
Dominant construction in Dongri is luxury glass towers above thirty floors, executed in red oxide flooring in old rooms. Façades range from weathered plaster stained by monsoon streaks to freshly painted societies in CIDCO pastels. Rooftops carry water tanks, antennae, solar heaters and pigeon coops; ground floors host shops, temples, garages and tea stalls. The agent should generate building footprints from Microsoft Building Footprints and OSM building polygons, extrude them using the SRTM/DEM ground height, and apply procedural façade rules (window rhythm, balcony rails, lorry loads, signage) so that no two streets look cloned. Heritage and Grade-I structures must use photogrammetry from Wikimedia/Mapillary rather than procedural approximation.

8. Landmarks, Civic Buildings and Public Realm
Anchoring the public realm of Dongri is a creek bridge with tidal mudflats beneath, around which daily life orbits. Additional civic anchors include schools, dispensaries, ration shops, ration-dependent chawls, police chowkies, post offices, railway stations or bus depots, and religious structures of every denomination. The agent should place these from OSM amenity, shop, office, place_of_worship and public_transport tags, and give each a believable interior hint (a ticket counter, a stepwell, a bell) so the world reads as lived-in rather than a film set.

9. Markets, Commerce and the Informal Economy
Commerce in Dongri is a stack of formal and informal layers: street vendors, weekly bazaars, kirana stores, wholesale markets (notably the APMC at Vashi and the power-loom/textile and warehouse economy of Bhiwandi), malls (Inorbit, Raghuleela, Little World, Viviana, Korum), and the heavy logistics of JNPT containers. The agent must simulate market rhythms - dawn fish auctions, midday lulls, evening crowding - with spawn tables tied to clock and weekday, and must scatter tractors on village roads as the prevalent moving load on the roads.

10. Residential Life, Communities and Daily Rhythm
The social texture of Dongri is dominated by Gujarati traders and Jain families, whose festivals, food and dress colour the streets. A typical figure one meets is a street barber with a mirrored chair. Homes are organised around shared wells, building compounds, chawl verandahs and society lawns; the agent should model domestic sound and smell (cooking, rangoli, drying clothes, evening prayers) as ambient layers so that the player, standing still, still receives a dense sense of neighbours. Caste, language and migrant geography should be readable in signage, shop names and the linguistic mix of NPC chatter.

11. Transport, Connectivity and Interchange
Mobility in and out of %s rides on the full Mumbai stack: the Western, Central and Harbour suburban railways; the Port line to Uran/JNPT; the Trans-Harbour and Panvel links; BEST, NMMT, TMT, KDMT and MSRTC buses; auto and taxi; the metro and monorail where built; and the road hierarchy from the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and NH-48/348 to the last village lane. The agent must lay track and stations from OSM railway geometries, animate trains on schedule, and let the player board, alight and transfer. Ferries connect koliwadas and islands (Gateway-Elephanta, Rewas-Mandwa, Uran creek boats), and a helipad/airport layer supports aerial movement.

12. Utilities, Drainage and Infrastructure
Under the surface of Dongri runs a lattice of utilities: BMC/CMC water mains, sewer and stormwater nullahs, MSEB/Torrent power lines, gas pipelines, telecom ducts and CCTV. The agent should render manholes, transformer yards, overhead cable forests and pump houses, and must model the ponds that form on laterite flats that defines monsoon realism. Power-cut behaviour (generator hum, inverter beeps) should trigger on a believable schedule so the grid feels alive and fragile.

13. Soundscape and Smellscape
Stand in Dongri and the ear receives the tinny speaker of a vada-pav cart; the nose meets the brackish tang of the creek at low tide. These channels are as important as the visual for 'real-world feel'. The agent should build a 3D ambient audio system with distance attenuation, occlusion by buildings, and a diurnal mix (call to prayer, train horns, market cries, festival drums, aircraft on approach). A parallel smell/particulate layer (visible haze, incense, diesel) should tint the screen subtly so the player's senses are saturated the way a real Mumbaikar's are.

14. Day Cycle, Lighting and Night Behaviour
Light in Dongri moves from harsh white noon to diya and lantern glow at festival after dark. The agent must implement a physically based sun and moon arc for the latitude (19 N), with golden-hour warmth over the creek and blue-hour city glow. Night brings different NPC behaviour: food stalls ignite, watchmen patrol, lovers walk the sea face, and the port works in shifts. Neon, diya, tube-light and navigation lights must reflect off wet tar and water with believable bloom and caustics.

15. Monsoon, Tides and Flood Dynamics
The signature drama of Dongri is water: ponds that form on laterite flats. The agent must couple a tidal model (semi-diurnal, ~4 m range in the Ulhas estuary) with a rainfall model (intensity curves from IMD climatology) so that low-lying reclamations, underbridges and creek edges flood realistically, while better-graded CIDCO nodes shed water. Mangrove belts should blunt wave energy; storm surge during cyclone alerts should temporarily submerge the lowest polygons. Pumps, sandbags and diverted traffic are part of the emergent gameplay.

16. Vegetation, Wildlife and the Edge of the Wild
Even inside the city, Dongri keeps a wild edge: salt-tolerant suru and palm belts, and - where the location borders Tungareshwar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Karnala or the creek mangroves - leopards, monkeys, peacocks, flamingos, kingfishers and crocodiles. The agent should seed fauna with believable ranges and schedules (flamingos in the Thane Creek flats, peacocks in Kharghar hills, leopards on the SGNP fringe) so the boundary between metropolis and wilderness is thin and thrilling, exactly as in the real region.

17. Human Density, NPC Archetypes and Crowd Physics
Population pressure in Dongri is intense. The agent must support thousands of concurrently simulated pedestrians with social-force crowd physics: a street barber with a mirrored chair jostles through a junction, commuters flow toward the station at 8 am, festival processions block roads, and personal-space bubbles part and re-form. Each NPC needs a simple daily routine (home-sleep, commute, work, market, leisure) drawn from the local economy so the crowd is purposeful, not random. LOD must cull and simplify distant crowds to hold framerate.

18. Vehicle Presence, Traffic AI and Parking
The road life of Dongri is a choreography of tractors on village roads. The agent needs a traffic micro-simulation: signal logic at junctions, lane discipline (loose), honking behaviour, overtaking on the wrong side, jaywalking pressure, and parking on footpaths. Heavy JNPT container trucks, BEST/NMMT buses, autos, two-wheelers, tempos and private cars each need distinct mass, acceleration and braking so the feel differs by vehicle class. Congestion should emerge from geometry, not scripting.

19. Implementation Notes for the Building Agent (data, mesh, texture, LOD)
To realise Dongri faithfully, the building agent should: (a) pull the OSM relation/way for 'Dongri' via Overpass using its bounding box; (b) clip the NASADEM 30 m and Copernicus DEM 10 m tiles to that box for terrain; (c) import building footprints from OSM + Microsoft Building Footprints and extrude to heights from OSM building:levels or a learned prior; (d) texture from Sentinel-2/Landsat seasonal composites and Mapillary street-level photos; (e) place vegetation, water and landmarks from OSM natural/water/amenity tags; (f) bake lighting and occlusion; and (g) stream the result with a quadtree LOD so the 1,000+ km2 region stays playable. Every coordinate should be re-verifiable against OpenStreetMap (planet.osm / Geofabrik Maharashtra extract) for roads, buildings, landuse, water, railways; the Overpass API (overpass-api.de / kumi.systems mirror) for targeted queries such as 'way["natural"="water"] (bbox)' and 'relation["route"="railway"]'; Nominatim for geocoding place names to coordinates; OpenTopography and NASADEM / SRTM 30m & 90m for elevation meshes; ALOS AW3D and Copernicus DEM where finer detail is needed; Natural Earth (1:10m coastline, roads, populated places) for the regional frame; Wikidata and Wikipedia dumps for landmark metadata; OpenAddress and Microsoft Building Footprints for parcel and roof data; Mapillary and OpenAerialMap and Sentinel-2 / Landsat-8 for imagery-derived textures; the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Applications Centre and CIDCO planning maps for node layouts; the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) and Indian Navy Notices to Mariners for restricted zones; and the Free Map Tools / bboxfinder.com for coordinate verification..

20. Player Experience Brief for Dongri
When the player arrives in Dongri, the intended feeling is recognition: the salt wind, the specific skyline, the exact slant of the flyover, the smell of the brackish tang of the creek at low tide, the sound of the tinny speaker of a vada-pav cart. The agent must not abstract this place into a generic city; it must be unmistakably Dongri, a slice of the real Konkan coast rendered at human scale, where one can walk, drive, sail or fly and feel the weight of a living, sweating, praying, working megacity that happens to sit on an island joined to the mainland only by bridges, creeks and causeways.

1. Identity and Precise Coordinates
Umarkhadi is a locality situated within the south mumbai micro-region of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. The character of Umarkhadi is shaped by its position: The southern tip of Salsette Island / original Seven Islands: Colaba, Mazagaon, Parel, Mahim, etc.

2. Etymology, History and Civic Evolution
The name Umarkhadi carries layers of civic memory. Historically part of the larger Salsette and Konkan settlement network, the place grew through phases of fishing-village economy, colonial port expansion, post-1960 industrialisation, and post-1990 planned node development under agencies such as CIDCO, MIDC and the Municipal Corporations of Greater Mumbai, Thane, Bhiwandi-Nizampur, Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Panvel. Oral histories, Marathi and Gujarati street names, and colonial survey maps (available via Wikidata and old Survey of India sheets) anchor the local identity. The agent should respect the real demographic layering when populating Umarkhadi, drawing on census ward maps and OSM landuse polygons.

3. Topography, Soil and Geology
Geologically Umarkhadi rests on Deccan Trap basalt of the late Cretaceous, overlain in low pockets by alluvium, marine clay and laterite. Power-cut behaviour (generator hum, inverter beeps) should trigger on a believable schedule so the grid feels alive and fragile.

13. Soundscape and Smellscape
Stand in Sewri and the ear receives the screech of mynahs in the banyan; the nose meets sweat and railway-platform tea. These channels are as important as the visual for 'real-world feel'. The agent should build a 3D ambient audio system with distance attenuation, occlusion by buildings, and a diurnal mix (call to prayer, train horns, market cries, festival drums, aircraft on approach). A parallel smell/particulate layer (visible haze, incense, diesel) should tint the screen subtly so the player's senses are saturated the way a real Mumbaikar's are.

14. Day Cycle, Lighting and Night Behaviour
Light in Sewri moves from harsh white noon to car headlights smearing on wet roads after dark. The agent must implement a physically based sun and moon arc for the latitude (19 N), with golden-hour warmth over the creek and blue-hour city glow. Night brings different NPC behaviour: food stalls ignite, watchmen patrol, lovers walk the sea face, and the port works in shifts. Neon, diya, tube-light and navigation lights must reflect off wet tar and water with believable bloom and caustics.

15. Monsoon, Tides and Flood Dynamics
The signature drama of Sewri is water: drainage that copes because of raised CIDCO gradients. The agent must couple a tidal model (semi-diurnal, ~4 m range in the Ulhas estuary) with a rainfall model (intensity curves from IMD climatology) so that low-lying reclamations, underbridges and creek edges flood realistically, while better-graded CIDCO nodes shed water. Mangrove belts should blunt wave energy; storm surge during cyclone alerts should temporarily submerge the lowest polygons. Pumps, sandbags and diverted traffic are part of the emergent gameplay.

16. Vegetation, Wildlife and the Edge of the Wild
Even inside the city, Sewri keeps a wild edge: casuarina windbreaks along the coast, and - where the location borders Tungareshwar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Karnala or the creek mangroves - leopards, monkeys, peacocks, flamingos, kingfishers and crocodiles. The agent should seed fauna with believable ranges and schedules (flamingos in the Thane Creek flats, peacocks in Kharghar hills, leopards on the SGNP fringe) so the boundary between metropolis and wilderness is thin and thrilling, exactly as in the real region.

17. Human Density, NPC Archetypes and Crowd Physics
Population pressure in Sewri is intense. The agent must support thousands of concurrently simulated pedestrians with social-force crowd physics: a vegetable vendor balancing a basket jostles through a junction, commuters flow toward the station at 8 am, festival processions block roads, and personal-space bubbles part and re-form. Each NPC needs a simple daily routine (home-sleep, commute, work, market, leisure) drawn from the local economy so the crowd is purposeful, not random. LOD must cull and simplify distant crowds to hold framerate.

18. Vehicle Presence, Traffic AI and Parking
The road life of Sewri is a choreography of private cars in bumper-to-bumper jam. The agent needs a traffic micro-simulation: signal logic at junctions, lane discipline (loose), honking behaviour, overtaking on the wrong side, jaywalking pressure, and parking on footpaths. Heavy JNPT container trucks, BEST/NMMT buses, autos, two-wheelers, tempos and private cars each need distinct mass, acceleration and braking so the feel differs by vehicle class. Congestion should emerge from geometry, not scripting.

19. Implementation Notes for the Building Agent (data, mesh, texture, LOD)
To realise Sewri faithfully, the building agent should: (a) pull the OSM relation/way for 'Sewri' via Overpass using its bounding box; (b) clip the NASADEM 30 m and Copernicus DEM 10 m tiles to that box for terrain; (c) import building footprints from OSM + Microsoft Building Footprints and extrude to heights from OSM building:levels or a learned prior; (d) texture from Sentinel-2/Landsat seasonal composites and Mapillary street-level photos; (e) place vegetation, water and landmarks from OSM natural/water/amenity tags; (f) bake lighting and occlusion; and (g) stream the result with a quadtree LOD so the 1,000+ km2 region stays playable. Every coordinate should be re-verifiable against OpenStreetMap (planet.osm / Geofabrik Maharashtra extract) for roads, buildings, landuse, water, railways; the Overpass API (overpass-api.de / kumi.systems mirror) for targeted queries such as 'way["natural"="water"] (bbox)' and 'relation["route"="railway"]'; Nominatim for geocoding place names to coordinates; OpenTopography and NASADEM / SRTM 30m & 90m for elevation meshes; ALOS AW3D and Copernicus DEM where finer detail is needed; Natural Earth (1:10m coastline, roads, populated places) for the regional frame; Wikidata and Wikipedia dumps for landmark metadata; OpenAddress and Microsoft Building Footprints for parcel and roof data; Mapillary and OpenAerialMap and Sentinel-2 / Landsat-8 for imagery-derived textures; the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Applications Centre and CIDCO planning maps for node layouts; the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) and Indian Navy Notices to Mariners for restricted zones; and the Free Map Tools / bboxfinder.com for coordinate verification..

20. Player Experience Brief for Sewri
When the player arrives in Sewri, the intended feeling is recognition: the salt wind, the specific skyline, the exact slant of the flyover, the smell of sweat and railway-platform tea, the sound of the screech of mynahs in the banyan. The agent must not abstract this place into a generic city; it must be unmistakably Sewri, a slice of the real Konkan coast rendered at human scale, where one can walk, drive, sail or fly and feel the weight of a living, sweating, praying, working megacity that happens to sit on an island joined to the mainland only by bridges, creeks and causeways.


================================================================================
LOCATION DOSSIER: Reay Road  (south mumbai)
================================================================================

1. Identity and Precise Coordinates
Reay Road is a locality situated within the south mumbai micro-region of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. Its generated reference coordinate is approximately 18.9056 degrees north latitude and 72.8376 degrees east longitude (verifiable and refinable through Nominatim and the OpenStreetMap node/way database, using the Geofabrik Maharashtra extract as the base layer). The area sits at an estimated mean elevation of about 410.0 metres above mean sea level, derived from the NASADEM / SRTM 30-metre digital elevation model and cross-checked against ALOS AW3D where finer relief is required. The character of Reay Road is shaped by its position: The southern tip of Salsette Island / original Seven Islands: Colaba, Mazagaon, Parel, Mahim, etc.

2. Etymology, History and Civic Evolution
The name Reay Road carries layers of civic memory. Historically part of the larger Salsette and Konkan settlement network, the place grew through phases of fishing-village economy, colonial port expansion, post-1960 industrialisation, and post-1990 planned node development under agencies such as CIDCO, MIDC and the Municipal Corporations of Greater Mumbai, Thane, Bhiwandi-Nizampur, Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Panvel. Oral histories, Marathi and Gujarati street names, and colonial survey maps (available via Wikidata and old Survey of India sheets) anchor the local identity. The agent should respect the real demographic layering when populating Reay Road, drawing on census ward maps and OSM landuse polygons.

3. Topography, Soil and Geology
Geologically Reay Road rests on Deccan Trap basalt of the late Cretaceous, overlain in low pockets by alluvium, marine clay and laterite. The terrain here is a pronounced hill plateau, with coconut and betel-nut groves as the dominant ground cover and basalt and laterite cut from local quarries forming the typical structural palette. Slope gradients should be sampled from the Copernicus DEM so that roads, drains and foundations follow believable contours; the agent must bake normal maps from the elevation mesh to give every lane and nullah a physically consistent fall toward the nearest creek or storm drain.

4. Hydrography and Proximity to Creeks, Rivers and the Sea
The hydrography around Reay Road is governed by the regional creek and river network: the Ulhas estuary gives rise to Vasai Creek in the north and Thane Creek in the east, while the Arabian Sea bounds the west and the Uran/Sheva and Karanja creeks shape the Raigad shore. Within Reay Road, storm-water nullahs, tidal inlets, ponds and (where present) mangrove fringes must be modelled from OSM water and natural=wetland polygons. The agent should render the ponds that form on laterite flats behaviour of water during the monsoon and spring tide, and must keep restricted naval and port waters (Butcher Island, Middle Ground, Oyster Rock, JNPT channel) marked as no-go zones using Indian Navy Notices to Mariners.

5. Climate and Local Microclimate
Reay Road experiences a tropical monsoon climate (Koppen Aw). Summers are hot and humid, the south-west monsoon from June to September delivers the bulk of ~2,200 mm annual rainfall, and winters are mild and dry. A typical atmospheric moment here is a cool December nor'easter off the sea. Microclimatic variation is real: creek-side and reclaimed lowlands are cooler and breezier, while dense concrete cores trap heat; the agent should drive a local temperature and humidity field from landuse (water, forest, built-up) so that the player feels the the brackish tang of the creek at low tide of each pocket.

6. Urban Morphology and Street Grid
The built fabric of Reay Road follows a regular planned sector pattern. Primary movement is carried by creek-side embankment roads with tidal views, with secondary lanes braiding into neighbourhood mazes. The agent must reconstruct the actual road graph from OSM highway tags (motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, service, living_street) and preserve one-way systems, foot-overbridges, level crossings and junction geometry. Where CIDCO planning exists (Vashi, Nerul, Kharghar, Panvel, Ulwe, Dronagiri), the sector grid with numbered sectors and central open spaces must be honoured exactly; where informal growth dominates (slum and warehouse belts), the organic, incremental lane network must be reproduced with believable dead-ends and shared courtyards.

7. Architecture and Built Form
Dominant construction in Reay Road is low chawl tenements with shared toilets, executed in basalt and laterite cut from local quarries. Façades range from weathered plaster stained by monsoon streaks to freshly painted societies in CIDCO pastels. Rooftops carry water tanks, antennae, solar heaters and pigeon coops; ground floors host shops, temples, garages and tea stalls. The agent should generate building footprints from Microsoft Building Footprints and OSM building polygons, extrude them using the SRTM/DEM ground height, and apply procedural façade rules (window rhythm, balcony rails, lorry loads, signage) so that no two streets look cloned. Heritage and Grade-I structures must use photogrammetry from Wikimedia/Mapillary rather than procedural approximation.

8. Landmarks, Civic Buildings and Public Realm
Anchoring the public realm of Reay Road is a creek bridge with tidal mudflats beneath, around which daily life orbits. Additional civic anchors include schools, dispensaries, ration shops, ration-dependent chawls, police chowkies, post offices, railway stations or bus depots, and religious structures of every denomination. The agent should place these from OSM amenity, shop, office, place_of_worship and public_transport tags, and give each a believable interior hint (a ticket counter, a stepwell, a bell) so the world reads as lived-in rather than a film set.

9. Markets, Commerce and the Informal Economy
Commerce in Reay Road is a stack of formal and informal layers: street vendors, weekly bazaars, kirana stores, wholesale markets (notably the APMC at Vashi and the power-loom/textile and warehouse economy of Bhiwandi), malls (Inorbit, Raghuleela, Little World, Viviana, Korum), and the heavy logistics of JNPT containers. The agent must simulate market rhythms - dawn fish auctions, midday lulls, evening crowding - with spawn tables tied to clock and weekday, and must scatter share-taxis hooting for custom as the prevalent moving load on the roads.

10. Residential Life, Communities and Daily Rhythm
The social texture of Reay Road is dominated by Buddhist (Navayana) colonies, whose festivals, food and dress colour the streets. A typical figure one meets is a fisherman mending a net. Homes are organised around shared wells, building compounds, chawl verandahs and society lawns; the agent should model domestic sound and smell (cooking, rangoli, drying clothes, evening prayers) as ambient layers so that the player, standing still, still receives a dense sense of neighbours. Caste, language and migrant geography should be readable in signage, shop names and the linguistic mix of NPC chatter.

11. Transport, Connectivity and Interchange
Mobility in and out of %s rides on the full Mumbai stack: the Western, Central and Harbour suburban railways; the Port line to Uran/JNPT; the Trans-Harbour and Panvel links; BEST, NMMT, TMT, KDMT and MSRTC buses; auto and taxi; the metro and monorail where built; and the road hierarchy from the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and NH-48/348 to the last village lane. To realise Cotton Green faithfully, the building agent should: (a) pull the OSM relation/way for 'Cotton Green' via Overpass using its bounding box; (b) clip the NASADEM 30 m and Copernicus DEM 10 m tiles to that box for terrain; (c) import building footprints from OSM + Microsoft Building Footprints and extrude to heights from OSM building:levels or a learned prior; (d) texture from Sentinel-2/Landsat seasonal composites and Mapillary street-level photos; (e) place vegetation, water and landmarks from OSM natural/water/amenity tags; (f) bake lighting and occlusion; and (g) stream the result with a quadtree LOD so the 1,000+ km2 region stays playable. Every coordinate should be re-verifiable against OpenStreetMap (planet.osm / Geofabrik Maharashtra extract) for roads, buildings, landuse, water, railways; the Overpass API (overpass-api.de / kumi.systems mirror) for targeted queries such as 'way["natural"="water"] (bbox)' and 'relation["route"="railway"]'; Nominatim for geocoding place names to coordinates; OpenTopography and NASADEM / SRTM 30m & 90m for elevation meshes; ALOS AW3D and Copernicus DEM where finer detail is needed; Natural Earth (1:10m coastline, roads, populated places) for the regional frame; Wikidata and Wikipedia dumps for landmark metadata; OpenAddress and Microsoft Building Footprints for parcel and roof data; Mapillary and OpenAerialMap and Sentinel-2 / Landsat-8 for imagery-derived textures; the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Applications Centre and CIDCO planning maps for node layouts; the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) and Indian Navy Notices to Mariners for restricted zones; and the Free Map Tools / bboxfinder.com for coordinate verification..

20. Player Experience Brief for Cotton Green
When the player arrives in Cotton Green, the intended feeling is recognition: the salt wind, the specific skyline, the exact slant of the flyover, the smell of jasmine and mogra from a flower seller, the sound of the screech of mynahs in the banyan. The agent must not abstract this place into a generic city; it must be unmistakably Cotton Green, a slice of the real Konkan coast rendered at human scale, where one can walk, drive, sail or fly and feel the weight of a living, sweating, praying, working megacity that happens to sit on an island joined to the mainland only by bridges, creeks and causeways.


================================================================================
LOCATION DOSSIER: Worli Koliwada  (south mumbai)
================================================================================

1. Identity and Precise Coordinates
Worli Koliwada is a locality situated within the south mumbai micro-region of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. Its generated reference coordinate is approximately 18.9162 degrees north latitude and 72.8041 degrees east longitude (verifiable and refinable through Nominatim and the OpenStreetMap node/way database, using the Geofabrik Maharashtra extract as the base layer). The area sits at an estimated mean elevation of about 126.8 metres above mean sea level, derived from the NASADEM / SRTM 30-metre digital elevation model and cross-checked against ALOS AW3D where finer relief is required. The character of Worli Koliwada is shaped by its position: The southern tip of Salsette Island / original Seven Islands: Colaba, Mazagaon, Parel, Mahim, etc.

2. Etymology, History and Civic Evolution
The name Worli Koliwada carries layers of civic memory. Historically part of the larger Salsette and Konkan settlement network, the place grew through phases of fishing-village economy, colonial port expansion, post-1960 industrialisation, and post-1990 planned node development under agencies such as CIDCO, MIDC and the Municipal Corporations of Greater Mumbai, Thane, Bhiwandi-Nizampur, Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Panvel. Oral histories, Marathi and Gujarati street names, and colonial survey maps (available via Wikidata and old Survey of India sheets) anchor the local identity. The agent should respect the real demographic layering when populating Worli Koliwada, drawing on census ward maps and OSM landuse polygons.

3. Topography, Soil and Geology
Geologically Worli Koliwada rests on Deccan Trap basalt of the late Cretaceous, overlain in low pockets by alluvium, marine clay and laterite. The terrain here is noticeably hilly, with teak and bamboo semi-evergreen forest as the dominant ground cover and weatherproof epoxy on port structures forming the typical structural palette. Slope gradients should be sampled from the Copernicus DEM so that roads, drains and foundations follow believable contours; the agent must bake normal maps from the elevation mesh to give every lane and nullah a physically consistent fall toward the nearest creek or storm drain.

4. Hydrography and Proximity to Creeks, Rivers and the Sea
The hydrography around Worli Koliwada is governed by the regional creek and river network: the Ulhas estuary gives rise to Vasai Creek in the north and Thane Creek in the east, while the Arabian Sea bounds the west and the Uran/Sheva and Karanja creeks shape the Raigad shore. Within Worli Koliwada, storm-water nullahs, tidal inlets, ponds and (where present) mangrove fringes must be modelled from OSM water and natural=wetland polygons. The agent should render the creek-side encroachment that worsens every surge behaviour of water during the monsoon and spring tide, and must keep restricted naval and port waters (Butcher Island, Middle Ground, Oyster Rock, JNPT channel) marked as no-go zones using Indian Navy Notices to Mariners.

5. Climate and Local Microclimate
Worli Koliwada experiences a tropical monsoon climate (Koppen Aw). Summers are hot and humid, the south-west monsoon from June to September delivers the bulk of ~2,200 mm annual rainfall, and winters are mild and dry. A typical atmospheric moment here is a October heat shimmer over the tar. Microclimatic variation is real: creek-side and reclaimed lowlands are cooler and breezier, while dense concrete cores trap heat; the agent should drive a local temperature and humidity field from landuse (water, forest, built-up) so that the player feels the the brackish tang of the creek at low tide of each pocket.

6. Urban Morphology and Street Grid
The built fabric of Worli Koliwada follows a regular planned sector pattern. Primary movement is carried by unpaved village paths hardened with laterite, with secondary lanes braiding into neighbourhood mazes. The agent must reconstruct the actual road graph from OSM highway tags (motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, service, living_street) and preserve one-way systems, foot-overbridges, level crossings and junction geometry. Where CIDCO planning exists (Vashi, Nerul, Kharghar, Panvel, Ulwe, Dronagiri), the sector grid with numbered sectors and central open spaces must be honoured exactly; where informal growth dominates (slum and warehouse belts), the organic, incremental lane network must be reproduced with believable dead-ends and shared courtyards.

7. Architecture and Built Form
Dominant construction in Worli Koliwada is heritage Grade-I stone buildings, executed in weatherproof epoxy on port structures. Façades range from weathered plaster stained by monsoon streaks to freshly painted societies in CIDCO pastels. Rooftops carry water tanks, antennae, solar heaters and pigeon coops; ground floors host shops, temples, garages and tea stalls. The agent should generate building footprints from Microsoft Building Footprints and OSM building polygons, extrude them using the SRTM/DEM ground height, and apply procedural façade rules (window rhythm, balcony rails, lorry loads, signage) so that no two streets look cloned. Heritage and Grade-I structures must use photogrammetry from Wikimedia/Mapillary rather than procedural approximation.

8. Landmarks, Civic Buildings and Public Realm
Anchoring the public realm of Worli Koliwada is a market hall with corrugated roofing, around which daily life orbits. Additional civic anchors include schools, dispensaries, ration shops, ration-dependent chawls, police chowkies, post offices, railway stations or bus depots, and religious structures of every denomination. The agent should place these from OSM amenity, shop, office, place_of_worship and public_transport tags, and give each a believable interior hint (a ticket counter, a stepwell, a bell) so the world reads as lived-in rather than a film set.

9. Markets, Commerce and the Informal Economy
Commerce in Worli Koliwada is a stack of formal and informal layers: street vendors, weekly bazaars, kirana stores, wholesale markets (notably the APMC at Vashi and the power-loom/textile and warehouse economy of Bhiwandi), malls (Inorbit, Raghuleela, Little World, Viviana, Korum), and the heavy logistics of JNPT containers. The agent must simulate market rhythms - dawn fish auctions, midday lulls, evening crowding - with spawn tables tied to clock and weekday, and must scatter water tankers and mixer trucks as the prevalent moving load on the roads.

10. Residential Life, Communities and Daily Rhythm
The social texture of Worli Koliwada is dominated by East Indian Catholic enclaves, whose festivals, food and dress colour the streets. A typical figure one meets is a senior citizen on a morning walk. Homes are organised around shared wells, building compounds, chawl verandahs and society lawns; the agent should model domestic sound and smell (cooking, rangoli, drying clothes, evening prayers) as ambient layers so that the player, standing still, still receives a dense sense of neighbours. Caste, language and migrant geography should be readable in signage, shop names and the linguistic mix of NPC chatter.

11. Transport, Connectivity and Interchange
Mobility in and out of %s rides on the full Mumbai stack: the Western, Central and Harbour suburban railways; the Port line to Uran/JNPT; the Trans-Harbour and Panvel links; BEST, NMMT, TMT, KDMT and MSRTC buses; auto and taxi; the metro and monorail where built; and the road hierarchy from the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and NH-48/348 to the last village lane. The agent must lay track and stations from OSM railway geometries, animate trains on schedule, and let the player board, alight and transfer. Ferries connect koliwadas and islands (Gateway-Elephanta, Rewas-Mandwa, Uran creek boats), and a helipad/airport layer supports aerial movement.

12. Utilities, Drainage and Infrastructure
Under the surface of Worli Koliwada runs a lattice of utilities: BMC/CMC water mains, sewer and stormwater nullahs, MSEB/Torrent power lines, gas pipelines, telecom ducts and CCTV. The agent should render manholes, transformer yards, overhead cable forests and pump houses, and must model the creek-side encroachment that worsens every surge that defines monsoon realism. Power-cut behaviour (generator hum, inverter beeps) should trigger on a believable schedule so the grid feels alive and fragile.

13. Soundscape and Smellscape
Stand in Worli Koliwada and the ear receives the tinny speaker of a vada-pav cart; the nose meets the brackish tang of the creek at low tide. These channels are as important as the visual for 'real-world feel'. The agent should build a 3D ambient audio system with distance attenuation, occlusion by buildings, and a diurnal mix (call to prayer, train horns, market cries, festival drums, aircraft on approach). A parallel smell/particulate layer (visible haze, incense, diesel) should tint the screen subtly so the player's senses are saturated the way a real Mumbaikar's are.

14. Day Cycle, Lighting and Night Behaviour
Light in Worli Koliwada moves from harsh white noon to the red aviation obstruction lights on tall towers after dark. The agent must implement a physically based sun and moon arc for the latitude (19 N), with golden-hour warmth over the creek and blue-hour city glow. Night brings different NPC behaviour: food stalls ignite, watchmen patrol, lovers walk the sea face, and the port works in shifts. Neon, diya, tube-light and navigation lights must reflect off wet tar and water with believable bloom and caustics.

15. Monsoon, Tides and Flood Dynamics
The signature drama of Worli Koliwada is water: creek-side encroachment that worsens every surge. The agent must couple a tidal model (semi-diurnal, ~4 m range in the Ulhas estuary) with a rainfall model (intensity curves from IMD climatology) so that low-lying reclamations, underbridges and creek edges flood realistically, while better-graded CIDCO nodes shed water. Mangrove belts should blunt wave energy; storm surge during cyclone alerts should temporarily submerge the lowest polygons. Pumps, sandbags and diverted traffic are part of the emergent gameplay.

16. Vegetation, Wildlife and the Edge of the Wild
Even inside the city, Worli Koliwada keeps a wild edge: teak and bamboo semi-evergreen forest, and - where the location borders Tungareshwar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Karnala or the creek mangroves - leopards, monkeys, peacocks, flamingos, kingfishers and crocodiles. The agent should seed fauna with believable ranges and schedules (flamingos in the Thane Creek flats, peacocks in Kharghar hills, leopards on the SGNP fringe) so the boundary between metropolis and wilderness is thin and thrilling, exactly as in the real region.

17. Human Density, NPC Archetypes and Crowd Physics
Population pressure in Worli Koliwada is intense. The agent must support thousands of concurrently simulated pedestrians with social-force crowd physics: a senior citizen on a morning walk jostles through a junction, commuters flow toward the station at 8 am, festival processions block roads, and personal-space bubbles part and re-form. Each NPC needs a simple daily routine (home-sleep, commute, work, market, leisure) drawn from the local economy so the crowd is purposeful, not random. LOD must cull and simplify distant crowds to hold framerate.

18. Vehicle Presence, Traffic AI and Parking
The road life of Worli Koliwada is a choreography of water tankers and mixer trucks. The agent needs a traffic micro-simulation: signal logic at junctions, lane discipline (loose), honking behaviour, overtaking on the wrong side, jaywalking pressure, and parking on footpaths. Heavy JNPT container trucks, BEST/NMMT buses, autos, two-wheelers, tempos and private cars each need distinct mass, acceleration and braking so the feel differs by vehicle class.
